title: Trace-experiment binding lookup must be unscoped, generic on failure, and fail closed
answers: how to check a trace belongs to an experiment before scoring
why batch_get_trace_infos should not use experiment_ids filter
what happens when the tracking store has no trace lookup
what error to return for traces in another experiment
body:
Invariant: _validate_trace_ids_in_experiment must call tracking_store.batch_get_trace_infos without an experiment_ids scope. Scoping hides foreign traces and makes the ownership comparison vacuous.
Fallback: per-trace get_trace_info runs only on MlflowNotImplementedException or bare NotImplementedError. RESOURCE_DOES_NOT_EXIST is treated as missing; any other MlflowException is re-raised.
Fail closed: a store implementing neither lookup raises, so the request is rejected rather than passed through unchecked.
Response: any trace whose experiment_id differs gets one generic PERMISSION_DENIED ("Not all requested traces could be accessed.") that does not reveal which trace or whether it exists.
applies: Changes to the trace-ownership check or to any new endpoint that binds trace ids to an experiment.
says: Evaluating model traces belonging to another experiment returns a generic permission denied error.
Prevent users from evaluating or accessing execution traces outside their current experiment scope.
Do not leak the existence or identifiers of unauthorized traces when scoring fails.
Trace evaluation requests must be rejected if the trace storage cannot verify ownership.
